text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

British Prime Minister and founder of the Metropolitan Police, SIR ROBERT PEEL, was born on this day in 1788. PEEL's concern about public safety led to the establishment of this first Police Force. Officers were called "PEELERS" and later "BOBBIES", after him.
American politician ADLAI STEVENSON, whose liberal views caused him trouble during the McCARTHY 'witch-hunts', was born in 1900.
American actor JOHN CARRADINE ("THE INVISIBLE MAN", "THE LAST TYCOON") was born in 1906.
WILLIAM BURROUGHS, US novelist, was born in 1914. Many of his books were based on his own experiences as a drug addict, including "The Naked Lunch".

US singer with 'Three Dog Night' CORY WELLS was born in 1942. The group was founded in 1968 and had several hits including "Mama Told Me Not To Come" (1970), "Joy To The World" (1971) and "Black and White" (1972). A comeback attempt in the eighties was unsuccessful.

Jamaican reggae singer BOB MARLEY, known for introducing reggae to an international audience, was born on this day in 1945. BOB was a cult figure of the reggae movement and had a string of hits including "No Woman No Cry" (1975), "Is This Love" (1978), "Could You Be Loved" (1980), "Buffalo Soldier"
(1983) and "One Love/People Get Ready" (1984). ERIC CLAPTON had greater success than BOB did with one of his compositions "I Shot The Sheriff".
British actress CHARLOTTE RAMPLING ("THE NIGHT PORTER","STARDUST MEMORIES") was born in 1947.

American singer/songwriter BOBBY BROWN was born in 1969. He began his career with the child group 'New Edition' in 1982. Their first success was with "Candy Girl" (1983) and further hits included "Cool It Now" (1984) and "Mr Telephone Man"
(1984). In 1986 BOBBY left the group and started his successful solo career. Hits included "Don't Be Cruel" (1988), "My Prerogative" (1988), "Roni" (1989) and "Rock Wit'cha" (1989).
** EVENTS **
1892 : The temperature in Siberia was recorded as
reaching 94 degrees F. below zero (-70 Celsius).
1922 : A new monthly magazine was launched in New York.
"READER'S DIGEST" was the brainchild of former book salesman DeWITT WALLACE.
1935 : Boxing Authorities in New York ruled that no bout
could go longer than 15 rounds.
1941 : ANDREW BARTON (BANJO) PATERSON, Australian poet
widely credited as the author of "Waltzing Matilda", died.
1945 : General MACARTHUR led American troops into Manila.
1953 : WALT DISNEY released the full-length cartoon film
"PETER PAN". At the time, it was decided to model the character "Tinkerbell" on MARILYN MONROE.
1957 : Rock group BILL HALEY AND THE COMETS arrived to a
riotous welcome in London.
1958 : Parking meters were introduced in London's MAYFAIR
STREET.
1967 : The ROLLING STONES appeared on Britain's 'EAMONN
ANDREWS SHOW' but had to change the words of their number-one hit"Let's Spend The Night Togther", to "Let's Spend Some Time Together" because of a Musicians' Union ban.
1974 : 13 year-old Swede MATS WERMELIN scored all 272
points in a basketball game.
1983 : Nazi war criminal KLAUS BARBIE was flown to France
to face a war crimes trial.
1988 : Russia's MIKHAIL GORBACHEV rehabilitated 21
'un-persons' executed and erased from history by former leader JOSEPH STALIN.
1989 : Media magnate RUPERT MURDOCH launched satellite
SKY-TV.
1996 : The Bosnian government told NATO it had arrested a
Serb general, a colonel and six other men for investigations into suspected war crimes.
